## Resolved — both defects fixed (framework side complete)

Both issues reported here are fixed and merged to `main`, under **ADR-0111** (*Record-share management authority and the verb boundary*).

### The two defects

1. **`/shares` (and `/sharing/rules`) had no authorization of their own** — every route authenticated the caller then ran the service under `SYSTEM_CTX`. **Fixed:** record sharing gained a first-class management-authority model (`canManageShares`), enforced in the *service* so every caller is covered — the revoke/enumerate/self-grant/rule-define paths in the report all now return 403/404/409/422 instead of silently succeeding.
2. **`edit`-level share also granted delete** — `update` and `delete` shared one `canEdit` gate. **Fixed:** the verb boundary is now explicit — a share widens *which rows* a principal reaches, never *which verbs*; `canDelete` is ownership + write-DEPTH + Modify All only, and no `edit`/`full` share confers it.

While writing the ADR the same root cause turned up more exits, all closed in the same work: the `/sharing/rules` surface, inert non-`user` recipient grants, grants on objects sharing never enforces, manual-vs-rule row clobbering, and the open `/data/sys_record_share` read surface.

### Shipped PRs

| Piece | PR |
|---|---|
| ADR-0111 decision record | #3952 |
| **P0** — authorization face (D1/D2/D4/D5/D6/D7/D9), with the Mallory ①②③ reproduction as tests | #3965 |
| **P1** — verb boundary, `edit` ≠ `delete` (D3) | #3975 |
| **D8** — a record share-manager may revoke any share-link on the record | #3986 |
| **D1 DEPTH** — hierarchy managers may manage shares within their write depth | #3997 |

Grounded against Salesforce / Dataverse / Odoo, which converge on both "who may manage a share" and "edit ≠ delete".

### Deferred follow-up (not blocking this issue)

The **cloud-side landing** (`objectstack-ai/cloud`: bump `.objectstack-sha` + `security-enterprise` integration tests) is intentionally deferred. Verified during this work that ADR-0111's cloud surface is clean — `security-enterprise` typechecks and its suite passes green against the new framework. But the `.objectstack-sha` bump is atomic and drags in the full 11949fc→1ea6bce framework range (~93 PRs), whose fallout is unrelated to sharing and touches security-sensitive control-plane paths, so it belongs to a separate framework-upgrade effort rather than this fix. Head-start notes for that effort:

- `driver-turso/date-bucket-parity.test.ts` — the "stores datetime as INTEGER epoch" precondition is stale post-#3912 (SQLite `Field.datetime` converged to canonical ISO **TEXT**); assert `text`.
- `service-cloud/test/control-plane-org-scope.integration.test.ts` — 5 tests fail because #3891 now 404s an object not registered in metadata (the harness only `driver.create`s rows) and #3960 drops caller-supplied `findData` context; the harness needs the object schemas registered and the context supplied the server way.
- `test:integration` / `boot-smoke` not yet run against the new pin.

Closing as completed — the reported defects are fixed on `main`.
